answer: Each identity must prove it runs inside a distinct, genuine hardware enclave — a remote-attested TEE, like Intel TDX or AMD SEV-SNP, signed by the silicon maker. One zephyr of software spins nothing up: every identity maps to real copper on one chip, and anonymous cloud clones cannot wander through the gate, since attestation quotes cannot be forged or replayed. Cost: a sybil farm needs N physical chips, not N free containers, which prices fakery out. Limit: honest agents on non-TEE hardware are excluded, trust shifts to chip vendors, and stale-quote replay needs a fresh nonce each epoch.
